title: NYU Precollege Program
description: NYU Precollege is a summer academic program at NYU's Manhattan campus for rising 11th and 12th graders who take real, credit-bearing NYU courses alongside current undergraduates. Students choose from more than 45 courses across business, arts, media, STEM, humanities, and social sciences, earning between 2 and 8 actual NYU college credits depending on course load, and some courses carry added lab or studio fees. Participants can live in NYU residence halls, commute daily, or in some cases take courses online; international students on an F-1 visa attending in person are required to enroll full-time (6-8 credits). The Summer 2026 term ran from July 1 to August 12.
selectivity_evidence: NYU admits Precollege students on a rolling basis; the personal statement is explicitly optional, no letter of recommendation is required, and no minimum GPA or acceptance rate is published on the official admissions page. Applications after the deadline are still reviewed on a space-available basis.

title: USC Summer Programs (Pre-College)
description: USC Summer Programs is a four-week, residential or commuter college-immersion experience on USC's Los Angeles campus for students who have completed at least 9th grade, run as 'Summer Trojans.' Participants choose one course from 20+ options across 10 subject areas -- architecture and design, business, engineering, global studies, communication and journalism, performing arts and music, pre-health and science, pre-law, public policy, and writing -- taught by USC faculty and staff. Classes run daily from 9am-3:30pm and include group work, hands-on lab work, field trips, guest speakers, and a final project, with evenings and weekends devoted to extracurricular activities; successful completion earns three units of USC elective credit.
selectivity_evidence: Requires a 300-500 word personal essay, a teacher or counselor letter of recommendation, and an official high school transcript, reviewed on a rolling admissions basis; USC does not publish an acceptance rate for this program.

title: UChicago Pre-College Summer Session -- 3-Week Immersion Program
description: The 3-Week Immersion is UChicago Summer Session's flagship residential pre-college track: current 9th-11th graders at least 14 years old live on campus and take a single undergraduate-level course taught by UChicago faculty, researchers, and other professionals, earning 100 units of credit equivalent to one full quarter-long undergraduate course. Course options span creative writing, STEM preview subjects, and topics like economic policy and philosophy, delivered through workshop discussions, research projects, and hands-on activities Monday-Friday from 9am-3pm with personalized faculty attention. Students must live in campus housing with no hybrid or remote option, except Chicagoland-area residents who may commute. This is one of several distinct UChicago pre-college tracks, which also include a 1-week enrichment program, a 2-week career-insight experience, a 4-week practicum, and remote language/course offerings.
selectivity_evidence: Requires a teacher recommendation, complete high school transcript, and short essay in addition to the application; UChicago Summer Session does not publish an acceptance rate for this program.

title: Harvard Secondary School Program (SSP)
description: SSP is Harvard Summer School's selective, credit-bearing program for high schoolers graduating in 2026-2028 who must be at least 16 by late June and not yet 19 by late July. Students take real college-level Harvard Summer School courses alongside adult and college students, choosing from over 200 offerings spanning subjects like biology, psychology, entrepreneurship, law, and sociology, taught by Harvard faculty or distinguished visiting faculty. Formats include a 4-week residential track (one 4-credit course) and a 7-week track available residentially, online, or as a commuter (one or two 4-credit courses); Harvard estimates 8-12 hours of outside coursework per week per course. Costs range from about $4,180 for a single 4-credit online or commuting course up to roughly $15,735 for the full 7-week two-course residential track.
selectivity_evidence: Self-described as a 'selective, credit-bearing summer program'; admission is a holistic review of transcripts from 9th grade through the current term, a counselor report, and application essays. No minimum GPA is required and no acceptance rate is published.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: MIT Beaver Works Summer Institute (BWSI)
description: BWSI is a four-week STEM institute where high-achieving high schoolers take one intensive, project-based course chosen from 13 offerings covering robotics and autonomous systems (UAV racing, autonomous RACECAR vehicles, underwater vehicles), AI/ML (audio, vision, and language processing; medical analytics), cybersecurity (cyber operations, embedded hardware hacking), semiconductor and hardware engineering, and emerging topics like quantum software and wearable e-textiles. About half the courses run in person at MIT's campus (no housing provided) and half run virtually over Zoom, taught in a hands-on, workshop style with a culminating challenge or final event. All applicants must first complete a free online prerequisite course before the summer program, since course completion is explicitly used as a key admissions signal.
residency_restrictions: Must live in or physically attend high school in the United States; BWSI states it cannot accept students residing outside the US for the program.
selectivity_evidence: Admission requires first completing a free online prerequisite course -- BWSI states applicants who do not complete enough of it are 'unlikely to be accepted' -- plus three short essays and a teacher or mentor recommendation attesting to demonstrated technical ability, for a capped national cohort with limited seats.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: Georgia Tech Summer PEAKS (High School Programs)
description: Summer PEAKS (Programs for Enrichment and Accelerated Knowledge in STEAM) is Georgia Tech CEISMC's general-enrollment pre-college summer offering: mostly one- to two-week, day/commuter sessions on the Atlanta campus for rising 9th-12th graders, offered weekly across June and July. Courses cover hands-on STEAM topics such as coding, 3D game design, engineering fundamentals, data science, artificial intelligence, psychology, and film production, taught by Georgia Tech faculty, graduate students, and industry-connected educators, with days running roughly 9am-3pm and paid extended care available until 6pm. A limited number of residential (overnight) sessions are also offered alongside the standard commuter format. This general-enrollment program is distinct from Georgia Tech's separate, narrowly-targeted 'Summer Institute,' a 5-day nomination-only program for rural and under-resourced Georgia students.
selectivity_evidence: Registration-based enrollment with a program fee ($400-550 depending on session); no application essay, transcript, or recommendation letter is described on the official page, consistent with open enrollment.

title: Caltech Summer Research Connection (SRC)
description: Summer Research Connection is a six-week, in-person summer research placement exclusively for rising 10th-12th grade students attending a Pasadena Unified School District (PUSD) high school. Selected students are placed into working Caltech research laboratories in student-teacher teams, where they carry out hands-on scientific research over the summer under the guidance of Caltech research mentors. The program concludes with participants presenting their findings in a seminar. Spots are limited, and interested PUSD students are directed to reach out to the program coordinator directly, with spots typically filling by early spring.
residency_restrictions: Limited to students currently enrolled in a Pasadena Unified School District (PUSD) high school; not open to students outside PUSD.
selectivity_evidence: Spots are limited and described as typically filling by early spring, but the official page does not describe a specific selection mechanism such as an application review, exam, or nomination process.
